meta.author: GVS = Geoffrey Verity Schofield, YouTube channel https://www.youtube.com/@GVS (channel id UCObA5o3mcc1felIMAv6cukw)
meta.method: We read titles, publish dates, descriptions and chapter lists from each video's YouTube watch page. Transcripts and comments could not be retrieved. For the 2025 creator tier list, we read the placements from the video's own storyboard preview frames. During each creator's chapter the frames show an on-screen name caption next to the tier board, so each new pick can be seen landing in its row. The last 6 creators (Israetel to Galpin) were filmed outdoors without the board on screen. We matched their segment photos to the final full board shown in Final Thoughts. The video says the order inside a tier does not matter and that his top 3 are in the pinned comment, which we could not read.
meta.verifiedVsSecondhand: verified=true means we confirmed the placements from the video itself (frames, description or chapters). verified=false means only the title, topic and tier names are confirmed and the individual placements are unknown. We found no usable secondhand write-ups (Reddit, articles) of the placements: web search returned none, and reddit.com could not be fetched.

tierLists.title: The Science Based Fitness Tier List (Who's Legit?)
tierLists.ranks: Science-based fitness content creators and researchers, ranked by legitimacy. On-screen title: 'The Science Based Content Creator Tier List'. Scale is S>A>B>C>D. His 10 criteria, shown on screen: 1 research and its quality; 2 'DYEL, bro?' (does the person lift and have a physique); 3 reasonable/nuance vs dogmatism; 4 how they react to criticism and whether they can change their mind; 5 science used as marketing (clickbait, drama, lab coats, rage bait); 6 educational background; 7 integrity/honesty; 8 selling out; 9 practical experience; 10 ratio of great to good to bad takes.
tierLists.notes: The 25 placements match the 25 creator chapters. We watched the first 19 land on the board during their own segments. The last 6 (Israetel C, Nuckols S, Barakat A, Warren S, TNF A, Galpin A) were matched by segment photo to the final board. A caption in Chris Beardsley's segment reads 'Also his buddy Paul Carter is D tier. If you block people that much for no reason...automatic D tier.' This was said verbally; Paul Carter is not on the board. Israetel's chapter is the longest (24:21-28:40). The description links a Lyle McDonald critique of Israetel and Kassem Hansen's Instagram 'rack pull debunk' of Milo Wolf. Later context: GVS posted 'The Jeff Nippard Situation Just Got WILD... (LATEST UPDATE)' on 2025-08-15 (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=L10lyWplTFY). We did not verify what it says, and Nippard's S placement predates it. The reaction video 'Mob Lawyers for the "Science Based" Mafia' by atlaspowershrugged (2025-03-20, https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=pvtBaewc_ek) is based on this list. We verified it exists but not what it says.

trustedCreators.name: Jeff Nippard
trustedCreators.why: Ranked S in GVS's 2025 list. GVS scored him 94.5/100 in 2020 and praised him for linking studies to his claims. He is the best single source for exercise-technique tutorials with cited hypertrophy research, and he also publishes programs. GVS's one caveat is that his RIR/RPE estimates may be optimistic.

trustedCreators.name: Dr. Eric Helms
trustedCreators.why: Ranked S by GVS. He is a PhD researcher and competitive natural bodybuilder, and co-founded Iron Culture with Omar Isuf (per that channel's description). He is the best source for natural-lifter programming and contest or diet nutrition. He has no large personal YouTube channel, so his content is on Team3DMJ and podcasts.

trustedCreators.name: Greg Nuckols
trustedCreators.why: Ranked S by GVS. Stronger By Science publishes careful, nuanced research analysis on strength and hypertrophy programming, and GVS cites its articles in his own videos.

trustedCreators.name: Data Driven Strength
trustedCreators.why: Ranked S by GVS ('Data Driven Strength Guys'). The channel does research-driven discussion of training variables.

trustedCreators.name: House of Hypertrophy
trustedCreators.why: Ranked S by GVS. The channel summarizes hypertrophy studies, including exercise selection and range of motion.

trustedCreators.name: Joe 'Hypertrophy Coach' Bennett
trustedCreators.why: Ranked S by GVS. A good source for exercise execution, machine setup and practical hypertrophy coaching.

trustedCreators.name: Lyle McDonald
trustedCreators.why: Ranked S by GVS. He is a long-standing authority on diet and fat-loss physiology. The handle is tagged as Lyle McDonald by another creator and its description fits him, but it is not officially confirmed. His blunt, combative style is a known trait.

trustedCreators.name: Kassem Hansen
trustedCreators.channelName: N1 Education And Training (founded by Kassem Hansen)
trustedCreators.why: Ranked S by GVS. N1 focuses on biomechanics and exercise execution. The channel title spells his name 'Hanson'.

trustedCreators.name: Dr. Andy Galpin
trustedCreators.why: Ranked A by GVS. He is an exercise physiologist, best for general physiology and training-principle background rather than hands-on lifting tutorials.

trustedCreators.name: Dr. Eric Trexler
trustedCreators.why: Ranked A by GVS. He is a researcher, but we found no clearly verified YouTube channel for him, so use him for reference only.

trustedCreators.name: Dr. Brad Schoenfeld
trustedCreators.why: Ranked B by GVS. He is a leading hypertrophy researcher with many published studies on volume, load and frequency, but he appears mostly on other people's channels and podcasts.

trustedCreators.name: Menno Henselmans
trustedCreators.why: Ranked B by GVS. A research-literate hypertrophy and nutrition coach, also cited by GVS in his 2020 supplement tier list (on BCAAs).

trustedCreators.name: Jeremy Ethier
trustedCreators.why: Ranked B by GVS. His clear, animated technique tutorials are beginner-friendly. In 2020 GVS praised him for retracting a criticized video and apologizing.

trustedCreators.name: Dr. Layne Norton
trustedCreators.why: Ranked B by GVS. A PhD in nutritional sciences, strongest on protein, dieting and debunking nutrition myths.

trustedCreators.name: Dr. Milo Wolf
trustedCreators.why: Ranked C by GVS, who linked Kassem Hansen's critiques of Milo's rack-pull claims. Milo is a published hypertrophy researcher (lengthened partials, proximity to failure), so use his research summaries, but GVS rates his practical claims lower.

trustedCreators.name: Dr. Mike Israetel
trustedCreators.why: Ranked C by GVS, whose longest segment is on him and who linked a Lyle McDonald critique. RP's volume landmarks (MEV/MAV/MRV) and its many short exercise-technique videos are still widely used, but treat the entertainment and hot-take content with caution.

trustedCreators.name: Dr. Andrew Huberman
trustedCreators.why: Ranked D by GVS. He is a neuroscientist, not a lifting specialist, and the segment's visuals include sponsored product imagery. Do not use him for training or nutrition guidance in Forge.

trustedCreators.name: Alan Aragon
trustedCreators.why: Not on GVS's list. He is a well-regarded evidence-based nutrition researcher and educator (Alan Aragon's Research Review). The only YouTube channel found under his name is unrelated.

trustedCreators.name: Squat University
trustedCreators.why: Not on GVS's list. A physical-therapy-oriented channel covering squat, deadlift and bench mechanics, mobility and pain troubleshooting. Good for technique and joint-friendly cues.

trustedCreators.name: Alan Thrall
trustedCreators.why: Not on GVS's list. Practical barbell coaching; his how-to-deadlift and how-to-squat style tutorials are widely recommended for beginners.

trustedCreators.name: Calgary Barbell
trustedCreators.why: Not on GVS's list. A powerlifting coaching team with competition-lift technique breakdowns and programs.

trustedCreators.name: Juggernaut Training Systems
trustedCreators.why: Not on GVS's list. Strength-sport coaching with technique series for the squat, bench and deadlift, plus periodized programming.

trustedCreators.name: Natural Hypertrophy
trustedCreators.why: Not on the 2025 science tier list. GVS ranked it #2 in his 2021 underrated-channels list and linked it among his favorite channels in 2021. Good for practical natural-lifter programming.

trustedCreators.name: Geoffrey Verity Schofield (GVS)
trustedCreators.why: The author of these tier lists. He covers natural-lifter hypertrophy programming, exercise selection and progressive-overload strategy.
